February has **28 days** in the year 2100. 

Under the Gregorian calendar, a century year is only a leap year if it is evenly divisible by 400. Since 2100 is not divisible by 400, it is a common year.

Although the Gregorian rule drops most century leap years, some widely used reckonings (for example the proleptic Julian calendar and certain civil implementations that have not adopted the Gregorian century exception) treat 2100 as a leap year, so February in those systems contains 29 days.

speaker: b
name: Free
content:
The definitive answer under the internationally standard civil calendar (Gregorian calendar, ISO 8601) is **28 days**. 

While the obsolete Julian calendar would assign 29 days, global civil timekeeping universally follows the Gregorian system, where 2100 is not a leap year because it is not divisible by 400. 

Therefore, the agreed-upon standard answer is **28**.

While alternate or historical reckonings like the Julian calendar assign 29 days, global civil timekeeping (ISO 8601 / Gregorian calendar) exclusively governs standard dates. Under this standard, 2100 is not a leap year because it is not divisible by 400. 

The final, standard answer is **28**.
